source.title: Module 7 — Supply Chain Risk: source coverage, golden lessons and no-rework release gates
source.body:
## Purpose
Build **Module 7 — Supply Chain Risk** as the next fully release-audited module, using the **v6.0.1 synchronized Modules 1–6 baseline**, without repeating the earlier rework.

## Source scope / completeness
- Primary detailed source: the 2026 CSCP v5.4 risk module (155 PDF pages).
- Presentation: 20 slides, divided into Section A (risk management and supply-chain risks) and Section B (risk analysis and response).
- Flashcards: 22 defined terms across the two sections.
- The currently uploaded question bank does **not** contain a complete Module 7 set. **Write original questions; never reuse the bank verbatim.**
- Manual section ranges: A, pp. 8–62; B, pp. 63–140; appendix exhibits pp. 141–155 available for checking the original illustrations.

## Planned architecture (coverage-gate proposal; may change only after full source mapping)
- **Section A:** 12 substantive lessons + review. Risk/threat/opportunity; SCRM process, maturity, roles; known and unknown risk; appetite/tolerance/thresholds; strategy and risk plan; COSO ERM/GRC; ISO 31000, ISO 31010 and Guide 73; identification; risk registers; tangible, financial, intellectual-property, reputation and litigation loss categories.
- **Section B:** 19 substantive lessons + review. Internal/external risk types; qualitative matrix, urgency and evidence quality; distributions; EMV and cost incidence; sensitivity/Monte Carlo; accept/avoid/transfer/mitigate; preventive versus contingent response; strategic, supply, demand, process, environmental, hazard, financial, malfeasance and litigation response; BCMS, ISO 22301, ISO 28000, recovery and cross-partner continuity.
- **Integrated fictional capstone:** *Stonebridge Industrial Components — Disruption Resilience Decision Pack*; worked expected-loss mitigation choices, decision-changing sensitivity, hard gates, cross-functional implementation and recoverability.
- Proposed 10 purpose-built fictional CSV datasets and 31 topic-specific SVG models; exact counts freeze only after the coverage review.

## Explicit alignment — avoid re-teaching
- **M1:** risk consequences of forecast volatility, demand shaping, S&OP.
- **M2:** resilient network design, cyber architecture, supply-chain performance and financial metrics.
- **M3:** sourcing, sole/single/multisourcing, contractual risk allocation, product/IP issues.
- **M4:** MPS/MRP, inventory, capacity, quality and operational controls.
- **M5:** shipping routes, trade exposure, cargo loss, reverse-flow dependencies.
- **M6:** CRM/SRM, supplier qualification, concentration, strategic relationships and crisis communications.

Link to the authoritative earlier lessons; Module 7 adds formal exposure, priorities, responses, and continuity—not cloned explanations.

## Release-blocking checkpoints
- [ ] **G0 baseline freeze:** use v6.0.1, inspect live `QUALITY.md`, released module conventions and validator.
- [ ] **G1 full source-to-lesson matrix:** every meaningful section objective, exhibit, slide and flashcard term mapped, with no manual headings left orphaned.
- [ ] **G2 golden lessons:** A01 and quantitative B05/B06 at ≥500 original topic-specific words each, final lesson headings, relevant SVGs, operational flows, original Q/A and distractor rationale, genuinely worked calculation, both-width raster diagram QA.
- [ ] **G3 Section A:** all lessons + original review (≥10 Q), links, datasets, visual review, editorial/originality check.
- [ ] **G4 Section B:** all lessons + original review (≥10 Q), independent cost/EMV calculation recheck, scenario/decision gates.
- [ ] **G5 integration/capstone:** final assignment and *calculated* solution, data locks, sensitivity, glossary/navigation/cross-module handoffs, formula sheet.
- [ ] **G6 hardened validator:** explicitly register M7; enforce headings, ≥500 words, mandatory data links, calculation controls, process flows, answer-position balance, plausible distractors, capstone completeness, SVG/CSV validity and **raster visual QA**. Human read of every lesson.
- [ ] **G7 draft PR → approval → merge → CI/release:** keep the work off `main` until all release conditions pass; no premature tag/release.

## Lessons learned / special checks
1. Avoid repeating generic SVG layouts; topic-specific compositions must be inspected at standard/narrow widths for clipping and legibility.
2. Prevent answer-position bias across topic, section review and capstone questions; all four options plausible, all distractors explained.
3. Mandatory dataset links must be enforced (including the analogous Module 6 A09 link regression).
4. **Cost incidence and probability must be correct:** a *certain* mitigation outlay is not multiplied by event probability; probability-weight only event-contingent losses/costs and label all assumptions. Source examples that define conditional net-outcome cost require explicit treatment.
5. Hard ethical/safety/legal/security/continuity gates precede numerical ranking.
6. Check external standard versions and the difference between historical curriculum language and currently applicable standards/laws. Do not reuse broken/superseded external links.
7. No APICS PDFs, slides, flashcards, question bank, copyrighted diagrams, private client data, or internal source metadata in the public release.
8. Verify the release SHA equals `main`; do not confuse a passing CI check with a manual quality audit.

**Current state:** source review and blueprint completed. No incomplete public Module 7 folder or release has been published. Next operational action: finish G1 coverage evidence and develop G2 golden lessons before bulk authoring.
